newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight, Brokers sceptical over owner prospect.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight, Brokers sceptical over owner prospect.

text.p: Despite some reasonably steady caper and panamax fixtures reported on Monday, most brokers remained sceptical about prospects for any imminent improvement for owners in the dry cargo freight market.
Demand for tonnage from grain houses was relatively weak and leading charterers such as Cargill and Toepfer have little to offer.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) fell eight points to 1,459.
GRAIN - Brokers were said to unhappy about the number and accuracy of some of the talk circulating about the U.S. Gulf/Japan route.
It was thought safe to assume that Friday's report that Hanjin fixed 54,000 tonnes heavy grain with NSAC tonnage for April 13/23 at $24.85 no combo was correct.
However, no confirmation was available of talk that Continental had booked tonnage on this route on subjects at $24.50 combo for April loading.

South Korean charterers were said to have fixed Maria Bottiglieri 75,265 dwt on timecharter from the U.S. Gulf to the Far East, and Captain John L 64,584 dwt was also understood to have been fixed from the U.S. Gulf mid-April, but further details were not forthcoming.
Reports that Halla fixed Alpha Gemini 65,298 dwt delivery Santos end-April trip Far East could not be confirmed.

The NSAC controlled National Prestige 75,100 dwt open Port Talbot April 11 was understood fixed for short period business on private terms, and Halla was reported to have taken Royal Ocean 70,677 dwt delivery U.S. Gulf April 16/25 for four to six months redelivery Atlantic at $11,500 daily plus unknown bonus.

Very little news emerged about handy-size fixtures. New business quoted included IRISL 60,000 tonmnes wheat east or west Canada/Iran for May, and Danish charterers KFK 30/30,800 tonnes barley Denmark/two ports China.

Others included, Tradigrain 25,000 tonnes maize up river Plate/Conchan, Glencore 25,000 tonnes heavy grain Paranagua/SE Asia, and Garnac 15,000 tonnes maize U.S. Gulf/Puerto Cortes, all for prompt loading.

MINERALS - Caper fixtures such as Irongate 179,000 dwt delivery Cape Passero April/May for a trip via Brazil to Japan at $19,000 daily to K Line and Bulktirreno for 120,000 tonnes coal Hampton Roads/Ijmuiden also for April/May at $5.50 to Cobam were steady enough, brokers said.
However, some reported the caper market as lacking impetus with little fresh enquiry.

In the panamax category, there was a variety of rates reported from the east. Nippon Steel was thought to have failed with Topyield 72,394 dwt for an Australian round trip at about $12,500 daily, and K Line was believed to have booked a similar vessel in this trade on subjects at $12,000 daily.

Halla's reported fixture of Artemis 68,800 dwt delivery Pusan mid-April for a Nopac round trip redelivery Taiwan $11,300 daily or SE Asia at $11,000 appeared relatively weak, although Deiulemar was said to have conceded a firm $8,000/$8,250 daily for Irene Oldendorff 62,210 dwt delivery retroactive sailing Osaka March 28 for a coal trip via Roberts Bank to Taranto.
HANDY-SIZES - Martrade was said to have fixed a 38,000 dwt vessel Black Sea/Far East at an undisclosed rate and a 26,000 dwt vessel delivery Skaw for a trip via the Baltic to India at $9,400 daily.
Markos 38,054 dwt went to Concept Bulkcarriers delivery prompt Continent trip Far East, with the rate believed to have been in the low $12,000's daily.
Western bulkcarriers were thought to have fixed a gearless 36,000 dwt vessel from the Baltic to the U.S. Gulf on subjects at $6,750 daily.

In the east, BHP was linked with Zirje 48,000 dwt for an Australian round trip at $9,750 daily, NYK with Camellia Estrella 42,161 dwt for similar business at $9,100 daily, and Olympic Miracle 29,000 dwt was fixed on subjects by Pan Ocean delivery mid-April Singapore for a trip via Australia with concentrates to Japan, South Korea or China at $8,000 daily.

At 11445 GMT the BIFFEX futures were unchanged to 20 points easier than Friday's close. April and May traded last at 1,490, down 20 and 16 points respectively after trading 166 and 160 lots each. Total volume was 380 lots.
